candidates.name: Wes Moore
candidates.background: Governor since 2023 and the first Black governor in Maryland history; Army veteran (captain, 82nd Airborne, deployed to Afghanistan), Rhodes Scholar, and former CEO of the Robin Hood Foundation anti-poverty group. Beat Dan Cox roughly 65-32 in 2022 and won renomination June 23 with about 88% of the Democratic primary vote. Widely discussed as a potential 2028 presidential candidate.
priorities: Lower costs and raise wages for working families
Fully fund the Blueprint for Maryland's Future education plan

cost.label: Signed the Fair Wage Act accelerating the $15 minimum wage and allocated $218M to help providers absorb it (Wikipedia)

health.label: 'Healthcare is a basic right that every Marylander deserves'; behavioral-health coverage, protect community health centers (Ballotpedia)

housing.label: Housing Expansion and Affordability Act plus tenant protections, right to counsel in evictions, and an order to clear 5,000 vacant Baltimore homes (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Signed the Maryland Values Act barring immigration enforcement at sensitive locations; declined to send the Guard to the border; condemned the Abrego Garcia deportation (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Mixed: signed 2025 budget raising $1B+ via new brackets on the wealthy and a 2% capital gains surcharge, but paired with $2.5B in spending cuts after proposing corporate rate cuts (Wikipedia)

climate.label: 100% carbon-free electricity by 2035 and net-zero by 2045; POWER Act targets 8.5 GW of offshore wind by 2031 (Wikipedia)

education.label: Funds the Blueprint public-school plan ($500M first budget) while cutting the BOOST voucher program with intent to phase it out (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Leans prevention: community violence-intervention funding and the Youth Charging Reform Act, alongside tougher juvenile probation measures and police data-platform funding (Wikipedia)

repro.label: Backed the constitutional abortion-rights amendment, a $25M abortion access fund, mifepristone stockpiles, and a 2026 emergency-abortion hospital mandate (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Signed the Maryland Voting Rights Act (SB 255) banning racially discriminatory local voting systems and 'removing barriers to the ballot box' (NAACP LDF)

sources.label: Maryland State Board of Elections: general candidate list

candidates.name: Dan Cox
candidates.background: Constitutional lawyer and former state delegate (2019-2023) from Frederick County; father of ten. The 2022 Republican nominee for governor, he lost to Wes Moore roughly 65-32, then won the June 23, 2026 primary with 45% over Ed Hale Sr.'s 36% for a rematch. Endorsed by President Trump in his 2022 run.
priorities: Reduce and eliminate taxes and fees
Border security and fighting fentanyl trafficking
Restore police funding and public safety

cost.label: Pledges to 'reduce and eliminate taxes and fees' and to 'limit, cap, and, where possible, eliminate property taxes' to make Maryland more affordable (campaign site)

housing.label: Mixed: down-payment assistance and first-time homebuyer tax credits alongside cutting 'building costs and permitting burdens' (campaign site)

immigration.label: Opposes sanctuary policies; backs E-verify enforcement, 'Remain in Mexico', and ending catch-and-release (Ballotpedia)

taxes.label: 'Lower taxes, bigger paychecks': reduce property taxes and 'Reduce Inflation by Suspending the Gas Tax' (Ballotpedia)

climate.label: 'Unleash domestic energy resources' and 'eliminate the socialist Green New Deal' (Ballotpedia)

education.label: Expand charter schools, vouchers, and tax credits; opposes CRT and 'gender ideology' in curricula (Ballotpedia)

safety.label: 'Double pay' for police officers, restore 'full quasi-immunity', opposes defunding the police (Ballotpedia)

repro.label: Defends 'the right to all human life, from conception to natural death' (Ballotpedia)

democracy.label: 'Election integrity' via voter ID and hand-counted paper ballots; called for audits of the 2020 election (Ballotpedia)

health.label: Backs 'expanding healthcare choice, transparency, and affordability' and 'increased competition in the health insurance market' (Ballotpedia)

controversies.label: Arranged buses to the Jan 6, 2021 'Save America March' and tweeted 'Pence is a traitor' during the riot; continuously promoted disproven 2020 fraud claims (Wikipedia)
Introduced articles of impeachment against Gov. Larry Hogan over pandemic policies, rejected unanimously; filed unsuccessful suits against mail-in ballot counting (Wikipedia)

candidates.name: Andy Ellis
candidates.background: Baltimore Green Party organizer and former debate coach who ran for House of Delegates District 45 in 2018 (4.5%). Running with Owen Silverman Andrews on a ticket that rejects corporate and PAC money; his signature proposal is a statewide ban on data centers.
priorities: End the corruption of the two-party system

climate.label: 'Declare climate, environment, food, and water emergencies to ensure state and local government act with urgency' (campaign site)

education.label: 'Build out and fully fund our public education system so it truly works for all' (campaign site)

health.label: 'Maryland needs housing, education, and healthcare guaranteed as rights and not luxuries' (campaign site)

housing.label: Wants housing 'guaranteed as rights and not luxuries' and cites 'sky-high rental eviction rates' as a problem the two parties failed to fix (campaign site)

safety.label: 'Too many people are locked up, too many people can't afford to live here, too many people are left behind' (campaign site)

candidates.name: Cathy White
candidates.background: Factory production worker for about 40 years, including 35 years in a photofinishing plant, with long family caregiving experience. The Working Class Party's 2022 lieutenant governor nominee (ticket took 0.9%), now leading its 2026 ticket with Cathy Permut. The party argues 'the two-party system serves only the rich' but has not published specific policy proposals.
